clue.text: Part of destructive plague in particular place and time

blocks.note: a locus is a specific place or position
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A plague is being pinned down to one spot and moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague of locusts is a vast swarm, so a single insect is one member of that destructive horde.

clue.text: Endure letters giving indication it's time to retire

blocks.note: to last is to endure or keep going
post is mail, the letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with correspondence hinting that bedtime has come.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded at the end of the military day, and at funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call signals soldiers to retire for the night, so it literally announces bedtime in camp.

clue.text: Raise instrument, held up in court

indicators.note: in a down entry, something held up is lifted so it reads from bottom to top
the instrument sits inside the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument is delayed in a courtroom while someone raises an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise money or support is to collect it, as with a collection for charity.

clue.text: Relating to parts left after Act One is rewritten

indicators.note: a script that is rewritten has its material rearranged into a new form
the single letter comes after the reworked words, at the end

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A playwright redrafts the first act, and some bits are left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectional describes something made of or concerning sections, which are parts of a whole.

clue.text: In which one can relax over some pints?

definitions.text: In which one can relax over some pints?

blocks.clueFragment: In which one can relax over some pints?
blocks.note: surface reading: a pub where one unwinds over a few beers

blocks.clueFragment: In which one can relax over some pints?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a piece of furniture you lie on, resting on top of a quantity of liquid sealed inside

explanation.surface: It sounds like a description of a cosy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The pints are not beer: they are the liquid filling a mattress you lie on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed whose mattress is a sealed bag of liquid lets the sleeper rest literally on top of many pints.

clue.text: Broadcast if editor kept cool, in a way

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
'if' introduces a condition
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newsroom wonders whether the editor stayed calm during a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms fitted with mechanical cooling are kept at a low temperature, one particular way of staying cool.

clue.text: Peer among those qualifying

indicators.note: the word sits among the letters of the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A peer of the realm is found among the candidates who qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is one's equal in rank or standing, as in being judged by one's peers.

clue.text: Intelligence about a hot kingdom in Middle East

indicators.note: the word for intelligence goes around the other letters, surrounding them

blocks.note: brain means intellect or intelligence
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An intelligence report concerns a hot Gulf kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island monarchy in the Persian Gulf, so it is a kingdom of the Middle East.

clue.text: Excessive pressure, you said, in outfit

indicators.note: said means the word is taken by its sound when spoken, not its spelling
the sound-alike letter is placed inside the item of clothing

blocks.note: a dress is an outfit
the letter U is pronounced like 'you'

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you are under too much pressure in your outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion by threats or force, which is pressure beyond what is fair.

clue.text: As aids for driving, English tees were endlessly modified

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the preceding word is dropped
modified means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Golf tees in England get adapted to help with driving off the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: Driving suggests golf, which the tees support; but the driving is in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is steered with these wheels held in the hands, so they are tools that help a motorist drive.

clue.text: Accordingly, like legal practice, or one who works in it

blocks.note: so means therefore, accordingly
licit means lawful, the way legal practice should be
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentence weighing up whether something counts as legal practice or as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to legal practice: 'it' is the law, the field in which this person works.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is a British lawyer who advises clients and prepares legal documents, so works in legal practice.

clue.text: Court official as hard-hearted employer

indicators.note: something with a heart of this kind has it placed in its middle

blocks.note: a user is one who employs or makes use of something
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A court officer is described as a cold-hearted boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher keeps order and shows people to their places in a courtroom, one of its minor officials.

clue.text: Recollected recipes with accuracy

definitions.note: a phrase meaning accurate, standing in for the adjective

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cook remembers recipes exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split it as re-collected: gathered again in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precise is exact and correct in every detail, which is what having accuracy means.

clue.text: It could be Arles? No, another French city

indicators.note: the phrase says the following letters could become something else once reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A traveller guesses at a French city, rejects Arles, and settles on another.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city on the Loire in France, distinct from Arles, which is in Provence.

clue.text: Demonstrated, somehow, smooth fabric

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two words: staged a sit-in, which is one way of protesting
second meaning: a glossy woven cloth

explanation.surface: Someone showed off a sleek material in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing adverb warns that demonstrated is meant in a sideways sense: protesters demonstrate by occupying a place, i.e. they sat in.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a silky textile with a glossy face, and the two words sat in describe a protest occupation.

clue.text: Dine out with minimal cash in Paris? That's not appropriate

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
with means alongside, joining the next part on after

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a cent is the smallest euro coin, the currency in Paris

explanation.surface: Eating out in Paris on almost no money is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offending against propriety, so behaviour that is unseemly or not suitable.

clue.text: Malingerer might report this, as heard in region of France

indicators.note: as heard means the word is taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a malingerer fakes illness, so complains of a pretend ache

explanation.surface: A skiver's complaint, when spoken, names a part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: A malingerer pretends to be ill to avoid work: a sham pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a historic province in north-east France, famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Cautious about impassioned words providing assurance

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for cautious wraps around the other

blocks.note: wary means cautious
a rant is a heated, impassioned speech

explanation.surface: A careful person speaks up wary of emotional language when making promises.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee about a product, i.e. a formal assurance of its quality.

clue.text: What's illuminating, naturally, in paper, and easy to pick up

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
something light weighs little, so is easily lifted

explanation.surface: An enlightening article in a newspaper is easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests understanding, but it is physical lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight is the natural illumination given by the sun, as opposed to artificial lighting.

clue.text: After heading off gun injury, relaxed

indicators.note: once its head is taken off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the word with its first letter removed
a wound is an injury

explanation.surface: Someone recovers and unwinds after a gunshot wound to the head is avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to relax, so someone who has unwound has relaxed after tension.

clue.text: Soldiers with guns following leaders in African capital city, as it is

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so the initial of each word is taken
following means coming after, so the soldiers go after the initials

blocks.note: the initials of the three words
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed troops follow their commanders in a capital city of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it is' says the initials come from the definition itself: the three words both define and supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana, on the West African coast.

clue.text: As example of 27, it must be removed from city newspapers

indicators.note: the pronoun it must be taken out of the next word, leaving the remaining letters

blocks.note: the word with the letters of 'it' taken out
the press is newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A tree is ordered out of the city's newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is EVERGREEN. The 'it' in the clue does double duty: it is the letters taken out of city.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a conifer that keeps its foliage all year, a typical evergreen tree.

clue.text: Perform final act in theatre? It's painful

blocks.note: first meaning: sew up the wound, the surgeon's last step in the operating theatre
second meaning: a sharp pain in the side, as after running

explanation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests a stage play; here it is the operating theatre, where an operation ends with closing the incision.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon sews up an incision to finish an operation, and the same word names a sudden sharp ache in the side.

clue.text: Wife in top hat, replacing husband, that runs along bank

definitions.note: a descriptive clause for the noun, a path running beside a river

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife goes inside the hat
read as re-placing: the letter for husband is put somewhere new, changing the order

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife dons a top hat in place of her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing husband' looks like swapping H for W, but it means re-placing: W goes in after TO, and the H is moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A towpath is a track beside a canal or river, used originally by horses towing barges along the bank.

clue.text: Very pale, like one that sits and broods

blocks.note: as means like
a hen sits on her eggs to incubate a brood

explanation.surface: A pallid figure sits moping like a brooding person.
explanation.walkthrough: Broods suggests sulking, but it is a hen hatching eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means the grey-white colour of ash, describing a face drained of colour.

clue.text: New form of propane, in theory

indicators.note: a new form of a word is its letters made into a different shape

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A new kind of fuel gas works, but only in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in plans or calculations but is untested in practice, which is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Manner of playing piano, say, that's off pitch

blocks.note: first meaning: a musician's characteristic way of pressing keys
second meaning: in rugby and football, the area beyond the side lines of the field

explanation.walkthrough: Off pitch suggests singing out of tune; it means outside the playing field. In rugby and football, touch is the zone beyond the touchlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist's touch is their style of striking keys, and a ball out over the sideline has gone into touch.

clue.text: Gardener's wife right in front of area for putting kind of shrub

indicators.note: in front of means placed before, so these letters come ahead of the next

blocks.note: Adam, the first gardener in Eden, had Eve as his wife
R is the abbreviation for right
a golf green is where one putts

explanation.surface: A gardener's wife plants a shrub right beside the putting area.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardener is Adam, who tended Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes plants that keep their leaves all year, and the word also names such a shrub.

clue.text: What's embraced by the don is mindless pursuit of pleasure

indicators.note: something embraced is held within, so the word lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the four words, ending at the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: An academic is accused of embracing mindless pleasure-seeking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the philosophy or lifestyle devoted to seeking pleasure above all.

clue.text: Garment for upper body — or lower

blocks.note: first meaning: a knitted pullover, a jumper
second meaning: one that lows, i.e. a cow, here a breed from the Channel Island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like the opposite of upper, as in lower body; it is something that moos. Jersey cattle come from the Channel Island of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted top, and a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, an animal that lows.
